metaData.originalTitle: 对话李开复：别叫我们 “六小虎”，叫 “金钱豹”
metaData.title: A Conversation with Lee Kai-Fu: Don't Call Us 'Six Little Tigers,' Call Us 'Leopards'
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: In an in-depth interview, 01.AI founder Lee Kai-Fu reveals that after abandoning pre-training large models, the company pivoted to To B enterprise AI transformation services, achieving 250 million RMB in revenue in 2025 and over 1.5 billion RMB in orders for 2026. The company is preparing for an IPO and hopes to be called 'Leopards' rather than 'Six Little Tigers.'
metaData.summary: This article is an in-depth interview with Lee Kai-Fu, CEO of 01.AI, by LatePost. It details the company's transformation journey after abandoning pre-training large models in early 2025 and merging some teams into Alibaba. Lee Kai-Fu candidly shares the initial morale crisis, employee departures, and how he rebuilt team confidence through town hall meetings and securing the first major deal. The core transformation strategy is the 'Number One Project,' where Lee Kai-Fu personally acts as the 'Chief AI Strategy Officer' to open doors for enterprise leaders, providing a full suite of enterprise AI transformation tools based on Multi-Agent and ontology. The article discloses 01.AI's financials: audited revenue of 250 million RMB in 2025, orders exceeding 1.5 billion RMB in 2026, preparations for an IPO, and plans to become China's first profitable AI 2.0 company next year. Lee Kai-Fu also shares his views on the competitive landscape of large models, predicting consolidation among foundation model companies and emphasizing that the real opportunity lies in helping enterprises use AI to change their financial metrics.

mainPoints.point: 01.AI abandoned pre-training large models and pivoted to To B enterprise AI transformation services.
mainPoints.explanation: In early 2025, 01.AI transferred most of its pre-training and AI infrastructure teams to Alibaba, ceasing its pursuit of AGI. It repositioned itself as a To B company helping enterprises with AI transformation, with the core strategy being the 'Number One Project.'

mainPoints.point: The early transformation phase faced a severe morale crisis and employee attrition.
mainPoints.explanation: After the team restructuring, one-third of the office desks were empty, and the turnover rate was high. Lee Kai-Fu rebuilt team confidence through candid communication in town hall meetings and by securing the first major deal, ultimately weathering the most difficult period.

mainPoints.point: 01.AI has achieved rapid growth and is preparing for an IPO.
mainPoints.explanation: In 2025, audited revenue was 250 million RMB, with orders exceeding 1.5 billion RMB in 2026, nearly half of which is ARR. The company is dismantling its VIE structure, plans to achieve single-quarter profitability next year, and hopes to be called 'Leopards' rather than 'Six Little Tigers.'

mainPoints.point: The core product is an enterprise AI transformation platform based on Multi-Agent and ontology.
mainPoints.explanation: Products include a full suite of enterprise AI transformation tools and a dedicated management tool for top executives. The core is to help enterprises abstract their own systems so that AI can truly understand and assist in decision-making, ultimately changing financial metrics.

mainPoints.point: Lee Kai-Fu believes large models have zero stickiness, and the key to enterprise AI transformation lies in organization and culture.
mainPoints.explanation: He has not paid attention to model leaderboards for over a year and uses SOTA platforms to select models internally. He believes AI transformation can only be driven top-down, with bottlenecks lying in organization, culture, and strategic decisions, rather than pure technical capability.

keyQuotes: I hope in the future, people won't call us the 'Six Little Tigers,' but rather 'Leopards.'
If the market doesn't accept it, no matter how amazing the technology, it's worthless.
Only by getting big clients to sign contracts with real money can you go further.
If an Agent can't change one or more numbers in your quarterly report, it's just a vanity project.
01.AI is my greatest love and belief in the 45 years since my PhD—giving up was never an option.

relatedArticles.title: AI Transformation Levels L1-L4 for Software Companies: From Personal Tools to Business Restructuring (with Real Case Study)
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes an L1-L4 framework for AI transformation in software companies, ranging from personal productivity enhancement to business restructuring, using HuiSuanZhang as a case study to detail the critical leap from L2 to L3.

relatedArticles.title: Eliminating AI Metrics, Zero Layoffs! After an 82% Stock Plunge, Duolingo Charts an Anti-Silicon Valley Path
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article, based on InfoQ's in-depth interview with Duolingo co-founder and CEO Luis von Ahn, reveals the company's unique practices during the AI transformation wave, including canceling AI performance metrics, maintaining a zero-layoff policy, embracing vibe coding to empower non-technical staff, and persisting with a long-term user growth strategy despite a sharp stock price decline.

relatedArticles.title: Dialogue with Minglue's Wu Minghui: AI is Killing SaaS, But I Found a New Path
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Wu Minghui, founder of Minglue Technology, believes that AI Agents will replace traditional SaaS, with the value of software itself approaching zero. The future business model will be open-source software combined with AI models and services, and he shares the practice and insights of his multi-Agent collaborative office platform 'Octopus'.

relatedArticles.title: AI Quarterly Report 26Q1: OpenClaw, the OpenAI vs. Anthropic Showdown, and Self-Evolution | LatePost Podcast
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Through an interview with Silicon Valley VC partner Henry Yin, this article provides an in-depth review of key AI trends in Q1 2026, focusing on the Agent paradigm shift triggered by OpenClaw, the product competition between OpenAI and Anthropic, and the profound evolution of AI self-evolution and the SaaS industry.

relatedArticles.title: Li Xiang × Luo Yonghao! Li Xiang's Ideal: Using AI Technology to Give Ordinary People a Life of Luxury
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Li Auto founder Li Xiang delves into the company's strategic logic for transforming from an automaker into an AI and embodied intelligence company, technical breakthroughs in self-developed chips and full-by-wire chassis, and his predictions for the endgame of autonomous driving and humanoid robots.

relatedArticles.title: The Story Behind Lin Junyang's Departure: Growth and Divergence Between an AI Tech Lead and a Large Corporation
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep review of the departure of Lin Junyang, head of Alibaba's Qwen, revealing the deep-seated contradictions between the autonomy of top AI talent and the hierarchical management and strategic synergy of large corporations.

relatedArticles.title: AI Agent Products Enter a Bizarre Phase: Everyone Is Building Luxury Goods
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Yubo argues that current AI Agent products are trapped in a cycle of serving the wealthy; truly useful products rely on expensive models, Doubao leads in the To C space but may not reach the finish line, while To B products capitalize on corporate anxiety, with courses and consulting being the most stable revenue generators.

relatedArticles.title: A Conversation with Dreametech's Yu Hao: My Real World
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article is a deep-dive interview by LatePost with Dreametech founder Yu Hao, systematically presenting the controversial entrepreneur's unique thoughts and practices on boundaryless expansion, the N+1 innovation methodology, brand premiumization, and constructing a new knowledge system to cope with an uncertain world.

relatedArticles.title: In Conversation with DJI's Frank Wang: Seeking Truth, Finding Freedom, and Living a Story
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: In his first in-depth interview after a decade of silence, DJI founder Frank Wang reflects on his journey from a brash 'genius geek' to a mature leader, exploring core philosophies on management, organizational entropy reduction, and technological innovation.

relatedArticles.title: Using AI for Meeting Minutes Is the Most Absurd Thing in This Wave of AI Transformation
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Drawing on the historical case of the Boeing 777 project, this article argues that the current practice of enterprises using AI solely to enhance individual efficiency (e.g., auto-generating meeting minutes) while neglecting organizational collaboration restructuring is essentially an absurd phenomenon of new tools being embedded in old workflows.
